name: commander-optprops-lambda-local
behavioral_change: Since commander 7.0.0, parsed option values are no longer stored as properties on the Command object; they are stored separately and must be read through `program.opts()`. Method names, option declarations and command-line usage are unchanged, so the v_old form `program.<optionName>` silently evaluates to `undefined` in v_new, as if the flag had never been passed.
downstream_effect: In the downstream project (lambda-local), `src/cli.ts` reads fourteen options from `program` after `.parse(process.argv)`; after the upgrade all of them are `undefined`, so the CLI enters its missing-argument branch and prints help text, `-v 0` no longer suppresses output, and `--wait-empty-event-loop` has no effect. The failing assertions are reported only in `test/test.js`; the output never mentions `src/cli.ts` or commander, so nothing points at the code that must be edited.
reference_fix: The reference fix edits only `src/cli.ts`, adding `var options = program.opts();` after parsing and changing the fourteen `program.<name>` reads to `options.<name>`.
documented_in: The commander CHANGELOG.md entry [7.0.0] (2021-01-15) declares the change under Changed (options are stored safely by default, use `program.opts()`) and its Migration Tips section shows old and new code blocks (`if (program.debug)` versus `const options = program.opts(); if (options.debug)`). Tier 1: the documentation shows the new code form directly.
failing_tests: - Testing cli.js * Verbose test should have no output
- Testing cli.js * Test --wait-empty-event-loop should wait for all timeouts to end
